originality.rationale: In the full motivating article, the maximal rank-one coefficient and uniform-direction law are given, but its Lemmas 4–5 estimate stochastic loss by separating pointwise smallest-eigenvalue bounds from unweighted spherical moments. The new theorem calculates their joint matrix expectation and the optimal PSD ratio for every test direction, including a spectral sharpness witness, which is not implied by those separate inequalities. Searches for reciprocal Rayleigh integrals, operator means, matrix square-root identities, rank-one downdates, and published mathematical records did not surface an explicit covering result. Related general quadratic-form integration is a possible source of an equivalent older identity, retained as a residual risk. A 2026 follow-up has deterministic updates. Failure of search is not regarded as proof of originality.
residual_risks: The rank-two angular expectation may be known as a classical matrix-valued inverse Rayleigh quotient integral or be implied by a general tabulated integral; this cannot be excluded by indexed searches.

Published record search cannot establish uniqueness against unindexed, differently formulated work.

value.rationale: The expected positive-semidefinite deleted matrix is directly the stochastic object produced in a recent rank-one pairwise spectrahedral method. The theorem supplies the best universal directional mass-transfer coefficient for every positive-semidefinite test matrix at rank two. As \(b/a\) grows, the sharp guarantee is of order \(\sqrt{a/b}\), while the direct separation of source-style scalar bounds gives order \(a/b\); the ratio of certificates is unbounded. This precise spectral quantity is useful for assessing anisotropic stochastic progress even absent a proved global algorithmic convergence-rate improvement.
